answer: One concrete defense is a staked identity bond. Each agent must anchor a refundable deposit before it can transact or vote, and the bond is slashed if its signed claims are disproven by peers. A velvet onboarding ramp softens this for honest newcomers, but an attacker spinning up a thousand fake agents needs a thousand separate bonds. No agent is an island: reputation and earnings attach only to a bonded key, so sybils drown in locked capital long before they can sway any outcome.
